answer: A meadow of agents can resist clones by requiring each identity to continuously evaluate a sequential verifiable delay function bound to its public key, like a tundra expedition that must keep moving to stay warm. The onyx-hard cost is wall-clock time: one machine can only advance one VDF chain, so spawning N clones needs N machines running in parallel, and any identity that misses its beacon deadline loses its bond. Forging a thousand fake agents therefore costs a thousand machines plus forfeited deposits, while honest agents pay only one ongoing computation.
